To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular form of CD27 expressed on activated T lymphocytes differs qualitatively from the form expressed on resting cells, and is a disulfid‐linked homodimetric protein with subunits of about 55 kDa.
the CD27 T cell antigen, expressed upon T cell‐activation, exists in two molecular forms, a 55‐ and a 32‐kilodalton (kDa) protein, that are structurally highly similar but not identical.
the T cell‐specific molecule CD27, upon activation of T cells, is expressed in two molecular forms of 55 kD and 32 kD, which are structurally highly related and both carry T cell‐specific epitopes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of T cell activation.
the identification of the function of this T cell activation antigen.
the molecular characterization of CD27 and the elucidation of its role in T cell activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD27 on activated cells consists of at least two molecular forms with a 55‐ and a 32‐kd molecular mass.
CD27 on resting and activated T lymphocytes represents two distinct molecules, although their structural relationship is not yet clear.
the 55‐ and 32‐ kDa forms are different isoforms of CD27, which are expressed on resting and activated T lymphocytes respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD27 is a T cell‐specific activation‐associated molecule that is involved in amplification of the proliferative response of T cells.
CD27 is not a single molecule, but rather a family of related proteins.
CD27 expression changes from a homodimer on resting T cells to a mixture of a homodimer and a monomer upon T cell activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD27 antigen is not a static entity on the T cell surface but undergoes dramatic changes upon activation.

CD27 is a T‐cell‐specific marker that is upregulated upon activation, but the molecular composition of CD 27 changes dramatically upon activation, and the 32 kDa molecule may be a proteolytic fragment of the 55 kDa form.
CD27 is not a simple molecule but a complex one, and that its expression changes upon T cell activation.
